title: How to Grow Pothos Indoors ( Epipremnum spp.): Care, Cultivars, and Common Problems

paragraphs.heading: Factsheet | HGIC 1568 | Published: Jan 30, 2026 | Print

paragraphs.heading: Quick Guide to Growing Pothos
paragraphs.text: Native Range: China, India, Southeast Asia Light: Bright, indirect light; tolerates low light Water: Allow the soil to dry completely before watering Humidity: Prefers 50% to 70% Temperature: 60°F to 70°F nights, 70°F to 85° F days

paragraphs.heading: Quick Guide to Growing Pothos
paragraphs.text: Pothos is native to China, India, and some parts of Southeast Asia. Its natural habitat is warm and tropical, where the plant receives dappled sunlight and high humidity.

paragraphs.heading: Ornamental Features of Pothos Houseplants
paragraphs.text: As a houseplant, the leaves are typically a few inches long and stay whole. The leaves are slightly heart-shaped and shiny, and the vines will fill a pot to create a bushy look.

paragraphs.heading: Best Temperature Range for Growing Pothos Indoors
paragraphs.text: Pothos prefer a warm room, between 60°F to 70°F at night and 70 °F to 85°F during the day.

paragraphs.heading: Best Temperature Range for Growing Pothos Indoors
paragraphs.text: Keep them away from air conditioning vents in the summer and from windowsills and heating vents in the winter, as hot and cold air can cause the leaves to dry out and damage plant cells.

paragraphs.heading: Best Light Conditions for Pothos Houseplants
paragraphs.text: Pothos prefer bright, indirect light but will tolerate lower lighting conditions.

paragraphs.heading: Best Light Conditions for Pothos Houseplants
paragraphs.text: However, lower light may cause variegated varieties to lose some of their coloring.

paragraphs.heading: Plant becomes overcrowded and root-bound
paragraphs.text: Most plants can be repotted once every year or two, depending on their growth rate.

paragraphs.heading: Plant becomes overcrowded and root-bound
paragraphs.text: For more information, see HGIC 1450, Indoor Plants - Cleaning, Fertilizing, Containers and Light Requirements .

paragraphs.heading: Plant becomes overcrowded and root-bound
paragraphs.text: Stem cuttings can be easily rooted when placed in soil or water but should have at least one node to root properly. Barbara Smith, ©2025, Clemson Extension

paragraphs.heading: Pothos Propagation
paragraphs.text: Stem cuttings can be easily rooted when placed in soil or water, but they should have at least one node to root properly.

paragraphs.heading: Water and Humidity Needs for Pothos Plants
paragraphs.text: Soil should be allowed to dry between each watering. Make sure to thoroughly water the plant so that water will reach all the roots.

paragraphs.heading: Average home range: 30 to 60%
paragraphs.text: Pothos will tolerate these low humidity levels, but humidity can also be supplemented with a humidifier.

paragraphs.heading: Average home range: 30 to 60%
paragraphs.text: For more information, see HGIC 1459, Indoor Plants - Watering .

paragraphs.heading: Common Diseases and Nutrient Problems in Pothos
paragraphs.text: Root rot: Common houseplant issue caused by overwatering or poorly draining soil. Using a well-draining soil mix and proper watering practices will help prevent root rot.

paragraphs.heading: Common Diseases and Nutrient Problems in Pothos
paragraphs.text: Yellow leaves: Often caused by overwatering or low fertility. Correct by fertilizing with a houseplant fertilizer every other month during the spring and summer.

paragraphs.heading: Common Diseases and Nutrient Problems in Pothos
paragraphs.text: Leaf Scorch and tip dieback: Often caused by low humidity or intense light. Ensure the plant is getting bright, indirect light and high humidity.

paragraphs.heading: Common Pests of Pothos Plants
paragraphs.text: Pothos are generally pest-free when kept indoors, but may be affected by common houseplant pests such as spider mites and mealybugs.

paragraphs.heading: Common Pests of Pothos Plants
paragraphs.text: Is Pothos Toxic to Pets and Children?

paragraphs.heading: Common Pests of Pothos Plants
paragraphs.text: All parts of a pothos are mildly toxic if ingested.

paragraphs.heading: Difficulty swallowing
paragraphs.text: For that reason, keep pothos out of the reach of children and pets.

paragraphs.heading: Golden Pothos ( Epipremnum aureum )
paragraphs.text: This pothos has large, wide leaves with yellow variegation. In the wild, it’s an understory vine that climbs up trees for sunlight.

paragraphs.heading: Cultivars of Epipremnum aureum
paragraphs.text: Cultivars of Epipremnum aureum vary widely in leaf color, variegation patterns, growth habit, and light tolerance, making this species especially diverse for indoor use.

paragraphs.heading: Snow Queen Pothos ( E. aureum 'Snow Queen'):
paragraphs.text: Needs lots of bright, indirect light to ensure adequate growth

paragraphs.heading: Similar to Golden Pothos, but has more slender leaves
paragraphs.text: Tolerates lower light conditions than ‘Snow Queen’ and ‘Marble Queen’

paragraphs.heading: Shangri La Pothos ( E. aureum 'Shangri La'):
paragraphs.text: Interesting pothos with dark green leaves that curl and point inward

paragraphs.heading: Prefers slightly more humidity than other cultivars
paragraphs.text: Pearls and Jade Pothos ( Epipremnum aureum 'Pearls and Jade') has large white spots and leaves with both light and dark green speckling. Abigail Taylor, ©2025, Clemson Extension

paragraphs.heading: Cultivars of Epipremnum pinnatum
paragraphs.text: Cultivars of Epipremnum pinnatum differ in leaf shape, coloration, and degree of fenestration, with many showing their most distinctive features when grown vertically.

paragraphs.heading: Large, deep green leaves with cream-colored variegation
paragraphs.text: Deep fenestrations that add significant interest to the plant

paragraphs.heading: No variegation
paragraphs.text: E. amplissimum has long, blade-like leaves with a silver sheen to them. Mature leaves have a pointed tip that may start to curl downwards.

paragraphs.heading: Heartleaf Philodendron ( Philodendron hederaceum )
paragraphs.text: The main difference is that the leaf petioles on pothos are grooved, while those on philodendrons are smooth.

paragraphs.heading: Heartleaf Philodendron ( Philodendron hederaceum )
paragraphs.text: Silver Lady scindapsus is often mistaken for a pothos plant because of similar leaf structure and growth habits. Abigail Taylor, ©2025, Clemson Extension

paragraphs.heading: Scindapsus Species ( Scindapsus pictus )
paragraphs.text: Scindapsus are also more challenging to grow as they are more prone to pests and disease and less tolerant of overwatering than pothos.
